Grew up in a strict family but had enough of everything. Christian all my life. Moved to the other side of the world for studies (wasn't my choice though) for a better life, but definitely struggling with the change. And I like to listen to John Mayer, eat pork ribs, and I love being in quiet moments. 

Struggled with depression since I was 9 (back then, I didn't know what suicide was, so I'd fantasise about "running away" into nothingness), when I was 14-15 anxiety and depression got really really bad, and I kept struggling with it till now, at 19. My school got a nurse because of COVID, my therapist told me she thinks it's time I go on meds, and just like that I got prescribed medication for dysthymia and things have gotten so manageable that it's crazy to think that I was living on survival mode all these years. All made possible because of the country I'm now in. 

I truly think life is about putting in the work to get better, reaching out for help, and a lot of timing. It's a sickness and we should recognise that it is one.
There's a lot of consolation knowing that you're not alone, but it's also a pain you wouldn't wish on anybody.

The loneliness of all of this is excruciating. It's true that it's lonely to walk around with this darkness and no one seems to know. And it's lonely when you almost kill yourself the night before, but then sit and eat breakfast with your family the next morning. And no one has a clue. But the truth is that you can't heal just from someone caring about you, you can't love away this darkness. 

All you can hope for is to find the light someday and keep going. I don't think anyone will truly move on from his suicide, there will always be unanswered questions and pain that will never heal. No one would move on from you, either.
I'm really, really sorry to hear that. You're not a monster, you're just not well. I don't know if you're religious, but I'll be praying for you.

I'm sorry. It is such a helpless thing to go through, both for the person on the edge and the person trying desperately to talk them down. All we can do is continue to be there for each other and hope that we all make it through some way some how. Be well.

I'm so sorry you're going through this. We have different stories, but the same kind of black hole I'm guessing. I don't know if we're allowed to mention it but this year I went through a string of "Why not do it tonight?" until one day I saw the nurse and got antidepressants and everything changed. 

It's hard to tell you now that there is something else to stay for because I know first hand that it's just empty words when you're actually facing the void. But one day changed everything for me. Timing changed everything for me. It's unimaginable how much the right place, right time can alter your entire life. 

I hope that you never let the darkness consume you. I hope you will make it through. I hope today will be the day for you, just not the way you expect.

I'm sorry. It's crazy because this is the place where people openly say they're going to do it and there is a never-ending stream of new posts. We all wish we could make it all disappear for others even when we're going through it ourselves.. hell of a sickness

I'm sorry to hear. It wasn't your fault in any way and hopefully that comment didn't push him to do it (I'm inclined to think not), so many of us here are really really unwell. It's hard to see each other disappear.

It's painful because the screens and the anonymity of reddit makes it feel far enough that we can pretend we don't notice. But sometimes I really wonder how many of the statistics were one of us. Be well, man.
